items.title: John "Knocky" Parker Interview, 1963-08-28
items.q: We had, I remember, things by Kalkia Davenport and old Jelly Roll...

ctx.x: Yeah. And what kind of records was your family buying?

Well, there was a Miss Hazel Booth at Whittle's Music Company who would put aside all through the year all piano solos that would come in. We had, I remember, things by Kalkia Davenport and old Jelly Roll, lots of Jelly Roll Martin pieces and Clarence Williams, early Wildflower Rag and Argan Grindr Blues and Kansas City Stomp by Jelly, Seattle Hunch. And in the fall, when Daddy would sell cotton and all, we had money, we'd go to Dallas quite frequently. And then we'd go by there, buy all those records that she…
It was mainly piano music that they liked.
